archetypes.name: symbol-sweep
archetypes.rationale: The plan renames .larch-keepalive→.larch-session and deletes lib-larch-cache-touch.sh; undeclared callers outside the listed files would silently break at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: Grep the listed files and their immediate sibling scripts for every occurrence of '.larch-keepalive', 'lib-larch-cache-touch', 'larch_touch_executing_cache_root', 'collect_active_session_versions', 'write_keepalive_sentinel', 'LARCH_UPGRADE_FALLBACK_SESSION_ROOTS', and 'LARCH_SESSIONS_DIR' (pin-guard usage only). For each hit, check whether the owning file appears in the plan's change list; flag any file that references a renamed or deleted symbol but is absent from the list — these are missing plan steps. Also verify the plan's claim that CLONE_PATH is recorded only in .larch-keepalive by checking whether session-env.sh, source-env.sh, or any other script already writes it, since if it does the identity-record rename may be unnecessary or leave a stale second copy. Finally, check whether the plan accounts for any test-fixture file outside the listed test scripts that writes .larch-keepalive directly and would need updating. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: concurrent-prune-race
archetypes.rationale: The old pin guard indirectly serialized concurrent pruners; the new design removes it without addressing whether two simultaneous /upgrade-larch runs across worktrees can race on stamp-write + prune and over-delete.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether the prune step is atomic with respect to concurrent /upgrade-larch invocations from different worktrees: two runners could both enumerate the version-dir list before either writes a new stamp, compute the same keep-8 set, and both delete the same dirs, or one installer's stamp may be invisible to the other's pruner. Check whether upgrade-larch.sh holds any lockfile or uses any serialization, and whether the plan proposes any such mechanism. Also verify that the plan's 'best-effort stamp write' failure path — where the just-installed dir has no stamp and falls back to dir mtime — cannot cause that dir to sort below 8 already-stamped dirs and be deleted before the always-keep-ACTUAL_VERSION safeguard fires (i.e., confirm the safeguard fires unconditionally, not only after the sort). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: md-contract-gaps
archetypes.rationale: The plan says 'rewrite' for multiple .md sibling contracts without specifying new content; underspecified contracts leave the implementer free to write internally consistent but behaviorally wrong docs that pass review.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each .md file the plan marks as UPDATED — upgrade-larch.md, cleanup.md, session-setup.md, write-session-env.md, write-design-current-env.md, lib-resolve-implement-tmpdir.md, test-upgrade-larch-prune.md — read the current file and assess whether the plan gives enough specifics to rewrite it correctly, including the new invariants, the env vars to document (e.g. LARCH_CLEANUP_RETENTION_DAYS validation rules, install-stamp path and fallback ordering), and the removed guarantees to delete. Flag any .md the plan describes only as 'rewrite the contract' or 'update the paragraph' without specifying the new text. Also check whether test-cleanup.md (listed as NEW) has any content spec in the plan, and whether test-session-env-roundtrip.md (listed as 'remove two references') would retain any cross-references to lib-larch-cache-touch.sh that contradict the new behavior after only those two lines are removed. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
